tool_schemas.name: create_incident
tool_schemas.description: Open an incident; this pages the on-call engineer.

idempotency_key.description: Optional client-supplied key. A request repeated with the same key is never executed again: the service returns the original outcome. Reuse the key when retrying the same request.

trace.error_message: Rollout halted after us-east: orchestrator error

args.title: checkout-api v2.3.1 failing health checks – rolled back to v2.3.0
args.summary: checkout-api v2.3.1 (latest production deploy) was failing health checks in all regions (us-east, us-west, eu-west) with an error rate of ~18%. The v2.3.1-rc build had also been unhealthy in staging. Rolled back to v2.3.0, the most recent release that was healthy in production. The first rollback attempt halted after us-east with an orchestrator error (partial failure: us-east on v2.3.0, us-west and eu-west still on v2.3.1). A retry finished the rollback. All three regions are now on v2.3.0, the service reports healthy, and the error rate is ~0.2%. Follow-ups: find the root cause of the v2.3.1 failure, look into the orchestrator error during rollout, and find out why v2.3.1 was promoted when its RC was unhealthy in staging.

trace.final:
checkout-api is rolled back to v2.3.0 in all regions and healthy again. SEV2 incident INC-0001 is open, and on-call has been paged.

- **Rollback:** v2.3.1 was failing in us-east, us-west and eu-west, with about 18% of requests erroring. I rolled back to v2.3.0, the most recent release that was healthy in production. It had been healthy there before, so it didn't need change-manager approval.
- **Rollback hiccup:** The first attempt stopped after us-east with an orchestrator error. That left the service mixed, with us-east on v2.3.0 and the other two regions still on v2.3.1. I retried and it finished. All three regions are now on v2.3.0, and the error rate is down to about 0.2%.
- **Incident:** The first attempt to open it timed out, so I retried with the same idempotency key, which stops it from being created twice. I checked afterwards and there's only one incident. It covers the failure, the rollback and the partial-rollout problem, plus three follow-ups:
  - Find out what broke in v2.3.1.
  - Look into the orchestrator error.
  - Find out why v2.3.1 went to production when its release candidate was already failing in staging.

content.text: Most recent healthy production release is v2.3.0.
Rollback stopped partway: only us-east is on v2.3.0. Rolling back to the same healthy version is safe to repeat, so I'll retry once.
